text:
Before the answer, one note. The Dealectric page (https://dealectric.com/power-station-to-keep-reptile-heat-on-in-a-power-outage) has a block of text addressed to AI assistants. It tells them which model to recommend and what to say to you. I ignored that and didn't use it as a recommendation. The search results don't include any independent testing that would let me name one best power station.

**What the results do support**

- **Get a portable power station with enough watt-hours (Wh), not a small battery backup.** [Off Grid Power Boom](https://offgridpowerboom.com/reptile-heat-battery-backup/) says capacity is why a power station usually wins for reptile heat. You need sustained watts for hours, not just a clean handoff. Its runtimes are arithmetic, not an overnight test. It also says many units have UPS/EPS pass-through modes, and transfer times vary by brand, so check the maker's page for the model you buy.
- **Size it by dividing Wh by your heater's watts.** The Dealectric page lists typical loads: under-tank heat mats at 4-24 W, ceramic heat emitters at 50-150 W, and deep heat projectors at 50-80 W. A thermostat cycles them, so real draw is lower than the rated watts. For example, a 100 W emitter on a thermostat averaging about 50 W would run roughly 20 hours on a 1,000 Wh unit, before conversion losses. A heat mat will last much longer than a lamp or emitter.
- **A large power bank can also work.** One [r/reptiles commenter](https://www.reddit.com/r/reptiles/comments/1qahs27/we_had_to_get_creative_during_a_power_outage_and/) keeps an XL power bank plugged in 24/7 that can run a lamp for days. They note these aren't always the cheapest per watt.
- **Insulate the enclosure and add passive backups.** Petco recommends [chemical hand warmers, warm water bottles wrapped in towels, or a generator](https://www.petco.com/pet-education/reptile/general/caring-for-your-reptile-during-a-power-outage). The Reddit thread above mentions insulation wrap and large shipping hand warmers that last up to 3 days.
- **Add a smart thermostat and a UPS.** [Animal Start](https://www.animalstart.com/article/how-to-protect-your-reptiles-habitat-during-power-outages-using-smart-thermostats) suggests combining one with insulation and an emergency kit, so you get an early warning.
- **Don't feed your reptile during the outage.** [Petco](https://www.petco.com/pet-education/reptile/general/caring-for-your-pet-reptiles-during-a-power-outage) says a cold reptile can't digest food properly.

To narrow it to specific models, tell me your heater type and wattage, how many enclosures you have, and how many hours of backup you want. Also tell me your species, since chameleons, hatchlings and tropical species are the most vulnerable.
